messages:
lina_marketing: Quick ask for the launch blog + webinar: marketing needs a compact, reproducible bench packet that highlights warmup cost vs steady-state cost. Can runtime own a short handoff?

lina_marketing: We don't need a full paper, just an evidence-backed packet we can ship in the blog appendix and show 2 slides for the webinar.

lina_marketing: Desired deliverables (priority order):
1) 20-seed prompts (split short/medium/long) that are representative of web-app chat UX
2) 3 variants per model: fp16 baseline, q8, q4 (where available)
3) Warmup profile: first-5-token latency distribution (cold start) for short+medium prompts (target ~600 runs each)
4) Steady-state table: p50/p90/p99 token latency + tokens/sec at conc=1 and conc=8
5) Latency vs cost tradeoff chart (per-variant) for a simple 1k-token lamp-test (est cost per 1k tokens)
6) 8 sample output pairs (fp16 vs quant variant) for redaction-friendly production prompts, with 1-line notes if quality differs
7) Repro snippet (curl + minimal warmup command) and small metadata.txt describing instance, kernel tag, quant profile

lina_marketing: Deadline: ideally by EOD Mon (so we can finalize slides Tue). If that's tight, tell us the minimal subset you can do in that window.

eli_runtime: We can take this on. Couple things:
- q4 may not be supported for the larger model shapes; we'll report availability and fallback.
- 600 cold-run target per prompt/variant is doable but will queue GPU time; if we need speed we can drop to 300 for long prompts.
- For the cost chart we'll need the token accounting method you prefer (billing tokens vs model-internal tokens). Which should we use?

lina_marketing: Use billing tokens so the numbers map directly to pricing.

harper_sre: Please include these in metadata: runtime build id, GPU instance type, kernel sha, quant profile label (e.g., q8_02, q4_v1), and whether the run used oss kernels or custom kernels. Also include trace ids for the 8 sample outputs.

eli_runtime: Good call. We'll attach a small metadata.txt per artifact. For sample outputs: can marketing give a sanitized set of production prompts, or should we synthesize? Shadow traffic would be ideal but I know that's heavier operationally.

lina_marketing: I'll DM a sanitized set (will redact PII). If it's simpler, you can synthesize a couple to fill in gaps.

devon_runtime: I'll run the smoke tonight and post results here. Plan: smoke run (small sample) -> confirm model variants + quant labels -> full runs Mon -> artifacts uploaded to marketing bucket. If we hit scheduler/backfill issues, we'll call a scoped MVP: warmup short/med + steady-state conc=1 only.

eli_runtime: Repro snippet we'll include in artifacts. Example we'll add to the packet:

eli_runtime: ```bash
# warmup then single request (example)
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-v1-medium","input":"<prompt>","max_tokens":256}'
```

eli_runtime: For cold starts we'll instantiate a fresh worker per run to simulate a cold container boot. Confirm that's what marketing expects.

lina_marketing: Yes, fresh worker per run. Also please include a short 3-bullet methodology blurb we can copy into the blog (what we measured, how warmup was simulated, caveats about variance).

harper_sre: Also include a note if any runs hit fallback behaviour (e.g., q4 falling back to q8) so marketing doesn't misattribute numbers.

bench-bot: bench:queued job id=992003 by devon_runtime :eyes:

devon_runtime: Check-list posted here: 1) get sanitized prompt list from Lina 2) smoke tonight 3) full runs Mon 4) upload CSVs + metadata + sample outputs 5) ping marketing with link + brief summary (include any regressions).

lina_marketing: Perfect. Please @eli_runtime and @devon_runtime in the final upload. If you think the minimal MVP for Mon EOD is warmup short+med + steady-state conc=1 + 4 sample pairs, say so. We can defer long prompt sweeps to post-launch.

eli_runtime: That MVP sounds reasonable. We'll aim for full deliverables but will call out the MVP as a fall-back in the artifact README. ETA update after smoke completes (~2 hours).
